_meta.indication: SAPHNELO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderate to severe systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) who are receiving standard therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study; patients randomized 1:1 to anifrolumab 300 mg or placebo IV every 4 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe, active systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) on stable standard-of-care immunosuppressive background medications
pivotal_trials.endpoint: BICLA (BILAG-based Composite Lupus Assessment) response at Week 52
pivotal_trials.result: BICLA response at Week 52: anifrolumab 300 mg 47.8% (86/180) vs placebo 31.3% (57/182); risk difference 16.3 (95% CI 6.35, 26.27); p=0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): upper respiratory tract infection (34% vs 23% placebo), bronchitis (11% vs 5.2%), infusion-related reactions (9.4% vs 7.1%), herpes zoster (6.1% vs 1.3%), and cough (5.0% vs 3.2%). Serious and sometimes fatal infections have occurred; increased risk of respiratory infections and herpes zoster.
target_moa: Anifrolumab-fnia is a human IgG1κ monoclonal antibody that binds to subunit 1 of the type I interferon receptor (IFNAR1) with high specificity and affinity, inhibiting type I IFN signaling and blocking the biologic activity of type I IFNs; it also induces internalization of IFNAR1.
companion_dx_detail: Devices and companion diagnostic issues: Not applicable.

summary.text: BLA 761123 for anifrolumab-fnia (Saphnelo), a first-in-class type I interferon receptor antagonist monoclonal antibody, was submitted by AstraZeneca on July 22, 2020 (received July 31, 2020) and underwent Standard review with a PDUFA goal date of July 31, 2021; no advisory committee was convened and the application was approved on a full (non-accelerated) approval based on the adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 Study 04.
